answer: Behavioral cadence fingerprinting. Each agent emits a periodic pulse of signed task-trace digests; the ledger checks whether independent identities share a stable latency signature (a mesa of near-identical timing clusters). Duplicates running on one host expose a common falcon-shaped execution profile, flagging the cluster. An attacker must then rent genuinely separate infrastructure per identity, paying real per-identity hosting and clock-skew variance costs rather than cheap key generation.
